questions.q: In the Northstar Supply Co. project, why was a /composite request chosen over a full Bulk API 2.0 job for loading 6 vendor contacts?
options: At that small a scale, Bulk API 2.0's job-management overhead doesn't pay for itself the way it does for large volumes
Composite requests cannot create records at all
Bulk API 2.0 only supports deletes, not inserts
REST authentication doesn't work with Bulk API 2.0
questions.explain: Bulk API 2.0 earns its overhead at real volume; for a handful of records, a Composite request is simpler and faster to set up and run.

questions.q: Why did the project's Composite request set "allOrNone": true?
options: To make the request run faster
To bypass the need for authentication
So a bad row among the new Contacts doesn't leave some Contacts created and others missing — the whole batch succeeds or fails together
allOrNone is required on every Composite request regardless of intent
questions.explain: allOrNone: true makes the composite request behave transactionally, avoiding a partially-committed batch if one sub-request fails.

questions.q: What was the purpose of Step 2 (querying for the Account by name) before creating the new Contacts?
options: To delete any existing Contacts first
To confirm the target Account exists and obtain its ID, needed to link the new Contacts via AccountId
To check the org's remaining API limits
To authenticate the integration
questions.explain: The new Contacts need a valid AccountId to link to, so confirming the Account exists and capturing its ID is a necessary step before creating them.

questions.q: If the spreadsheet export instead contained 40,000 vendor contacts instead of 6, what should change about Steps 3 and 4 of the project?
options: Nothing — Composite requests scale to any volume with no changes needed
Switch to the SOAP API instead, since REST cannot handle large volumes
Switch to Salesforce Connect, since the data should no longer be stored in Salesforce
Switch from a /composite request to the full Bulk API 2.0 job lifecycle (create job, upload CSV, close, poll, retrieve results), since that scale justifies the asynchronous job model
questions.explain: At 40,000 records, the scale justifies Bulk API 2.0's asynchronous job model rather than a single Composite call with its 25-subrequest limit.

questions.q: In Step 5, what should happen if one sub-request in the Composite response fails with errorCode REQUIRED_FIELD_MISSING?
options: Fix the source data to include the missing field before retrying — this is a request-validity error, not a transient one
Retry the identical request immediately and repeatedly
Ignore it, since allOrNone guarantees it will eventually succeed on its own
Switch immediately to the SOAP API
questions.explain: Per Lesson 13's error-handling guidance, a REQUIRED_FIELD_MISSING error means the request itself is wrong and needs its payload corrected, not blindly retried.
